context.body: Now King David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.

observations.body: David’s age, Abishag’s service, Adonijah’s self-exaltation, invited supporters, excluded figures, and Nathan and Bathsheba’s coordinated appeal bring the succession crisis to the king.
observations.label: Adonijah advances while David is old: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, Abishag, Adonijah, Joab, Abiathar, Nathan, Bathsheba, Solomon, and invited sons, the royal chamber, En Rogel, and Jerusalem, serving, exalting, preparing chariots, sacrificing, excluding, warning, entering, and questioning visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Adonijah advances while David is old: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: David, Abishag, Adonijah, Joab, Abiathar, Nathan, Bathsheba, Solomon, and invited sons · the royal chamber, En Rogel, and Jerusalem · serving, exalting, preparing chariots, sacrificing, excluding, warning, entering, and questioning · silence about succession allows a rival claim to gather publicly
observations.label: Relationships named in 1 Kings 1:1–27

payload.posture: Read 1 Kings 1:1–27 as its own succession, retelling, and temple preparation David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places silence about succession allows a rival claim to gather publicly inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: Adonijah advances while David is old
